name: Deferrable background work (WorkManager, JobScheduler)
plain: The standard way to run background tasks; periodic work cannot repeat faster than every 15 minutes.
meaning: Defines how often a background sync can run for an idle install. The 15 minute minimum and bucket quotas make exact timing impossible, so apps lean on push for freshness.

android.persistence: Persisted across reboots by WorkManager; constraints decide start
android.note: Periodic minimum interval 15 min (flex window 5 min); regular job quotas by bucket; Android 16 adds top state and FGS quota enforcement

ios.persistence: System decides when; earliestBeginDate is only a lower bound
ios.note: iOS has no guaranteed interval; see mob.bg.ios-refresh-processing

limits.headline: Can run background jobs on Android, but not more often than every 15 minutes
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app sets up a sync, upload or cleanup job
can: Run a job on a schedule, such as every 15 minutes or longer
Wait for good conditions, like Wi-Fi or charging
Retry later if a job fails
cannot: Run at an exact second; the system picks a good time
Use up the quota for its group; jobs get fewer minutes when the app is rarely opened
Count on a guaranteed time on iPhone, which has no fixed interval
limits.differs: Android has a standard job system with a 15 minute minimum. iPhone has no guaranteed interval.

story.what_it_is: The standard way for Android apps to run tasks later in the background, no faster than every 15 minutes.

marketing.name: WorkManager
marketing.pitch: Google pitches WorkManager as the recommended solution for reliable background work that must run even if the app exits.

story.for_you: You never see it. Photos back up, drafts send and data syncs when your phone has network or charge. It might finish late, but it should finish.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for uploads, sync and cleanup that must not be lost. Since the timing is loose, they use push messages when freshness matters.

use_cases.example: A photo app uploads new pictures when you are on Wi-Fi and plugged in.
A chat app retries a message that failed to send when the signal returns.
A notes app saves your offline edits to the server when you reconnect.
A fitness app uploads your workout file after you finish and go online.
An ad or analytics SDK batches events and sends them in scheduled jobs.
A game downloads new level files in the background overnight.

risks: Can be used to poll for signals
story.android_note: Periodic work cannot repeat faster than 15 minutes. Quotas depend on the standby group.
story.ios_note: iOS has no guaranteed interval. Apps use app refresh and processing tasks.

technical_bounds: Cannot run more often than every 15 minutes

history.change: Quotas also depend on top state and foreground service; STOP_REASON_TIMEOUT_ABANDONED added
Task timeouts for dataSync and mediaProcessing (see FGS timeouts)
